meta.title: Thermopylae
meta.eyebrow: Late summer 480 BC · Malis · Greco-Persian Wars
meta.subtitle: A few thousand Greeks hold the gap between Mount Kallidromos and the sea for two days, until a mountain path turns the position.

sun.note: Herodotus ties the campaign to the Carneia and the Olympic games; modern dates run from August to September 480 BC [stronk]. The sun is set for about 1 September. Herodotus's own times: Hydarnes leaves 'about lamp-lighting', reaches the summit at dawn, and Xerxes attacks at 'the hour when the market fills' [hdt].

meta.strengthNote: Greeks: Herodotus's list (5,200 with 1,000 Phocians) plus 900 helots and 1,000 Opuntian Locrians = 7,100. Diodorus gives about 7,400; Pausanias up to 11,200 [hdt] [diod] [paus]. Persians: Herodotus's millions are impossible; 120,000 is the low end of modern estimates [wp] [kv]. The Medes' and Cissians' myriads (10,000 each) and the 20,000 sent in on day 3 are illustrative; only the Immortals' 10,000 is a source figure [hdt]. Losses follow Herodotus's 20,000 Persian dead and the modern figure of about 2,000 Greek dead [hdt] [wp]; how they are spread across the moments is an estimate. On day 3 the dismissed allies (about 3,700) and the Phocians (about 1,000) leave or stand aside; the Thebans (about 340 left) surrender.
meta.method: The 480 BC shoreline and the pass come from the Kromayer-Veith maps of 1922-29, which rest on Grundy's 1899 survey and the French staff survey. They are georeferenced to OSM's Phocian wall, Kolonos and old baths (map 6, 25 m) and to seven villages (map 5, 173 m) [kv] [data]. The vanished water is drawn over today's Spercheios plain, and the ground inside it is lowered to sea level; it agrees with Grundy's 5-10 yard contour and the geoarchaeological reconstruction [grundy] [kraft]. Unit positions follow Herodotus's sequence on that ground [hdt]. The Anopaea route and the Phocian post are one reconstruction among several, and are low confidence [kv] [standrews].
meta.notes: The pass at the Middle Gate was some 15-30 m wide in 480; at this map's 43 m grid it shows as a strip, and the units' frontages are drawn wider than the hoplite files would have been. Today's shore lies 1-8 km further north [stronk]. The Anopaea route shown runs up from the Asopus crossing by Kalkomata and Paleo-Eleftherochori, through the Nevropoli meadows, over the Sastani saddle and down the Alpenoi ravine. Kromayer's shorter line via Alt-Damasta, and Leake's and Grundy's variants, are described in the debate notes. Diodorus's night attack on Xerxes' tent is not shown. The oak woods on Kallidromos are drawn schematically from Herodotus's 'all the mountain was covered with oak-trees'. Phocian and Locrian contingent positions in camp are illustrative. No historical-map overlay is offered.

phases.label: Day 1, dawn
phases.title: Two armies at the gates
phases.text: On the fifth day after Xerxes reached Malis, the Greeks hold the Middle Gate behind the rebuilt Phocian wall [hdt]. In 480 the sea came almost to the cliffs at three points; at the wall only a narrow strip of ground lay between Kallidromos and the water [hdt] [kv] [kraft]. The Lacedaemonians are posted outside the wall [hdt]. A thousand Phocians guard the mountain path [hdt]. The Persian army is encamped on the Trachinian plain beyond the Asopus [hdt] [panel].
tactic: Narrow front
A small army chooses ground so narrow that the enemy can only bring as many men into contact as it has itself; numbers and cavalry stop counting.
events: The rebuilt Phocian wall at the Middle Gate [hdt]
The 480 BC shore: today this is dry land 3-5 km from the sea [kv] [stronk]
Phocians guard the Anopaea path on the mountain [hdt] [kv]
phases.debate: Herodotus's compass is turned through 90 degrees: his 'west' is the mountain (south) and his 'east' the sea (north) [stronk]. The wall is placed where Kromayer's 1:25,000 map draws it, 190 m south-west of Kolonos; OSM's excavated wall segment agrees [kv] [data].

phases.label: Medes attack
phases.title: The Medes and Cissians come on
phases.text: Angry that the Greeks have not fled, Xerxes sends in the Medes and Cissians with orders to bring them alive. They lose heavily all day without breaking the line; fresh men keep coming up [hdt]. Diodorus says the Greek shields and close ranks beat the Persians' light wicker shields in the narrows [diod].
tactic: Narrow front
In the narrows only the front ranks fight; the Persian advantage in numbers counts for almost nothing.
events: The Medes lose heavily in front of the wall [hdt]
phases.debate: The time is illustrative: Herodotus says only that the combat 'went on throughout the day' [hdt]. Diodorus adds Sacae to the second wave [diod].

phases.label: The Immortals
phases.title: Feigned flights
phases.text: When the Medes are worn out, Hydarnes' Immortals take their place and fare no better: their spears are shorter and they cannot use their numbers. The Spartans turn their backs as if in flight, wait for the Persians to rush after them in disorder, then face about and cut them down. Xerxes is said to have leapt from his seat three times [hdt].
tactic: Feigned retreat
Drilled troops turned and pretended to run; when the pursuers broke ranks, they faced about and struck.

phases.label: Day 2
phases.title: The contingents take turns
phases.text: The next day the Persians attack again, hoping the few defenders are exhausted. The Greeks are drawn up by companies and nations and fight in turn, all except the Phocians, who are on the mountain [hdt]. Diodorus has picked men from every nation sent in, with whips at their backs [diod].
tactic: Rally and re-form
Rotating fresh units into a narrow front keeps the line strong while tired men rest behind the wall.
events: Contingents relieve each other in the line [hdt]
phases.debate: Herodotus does not say which contingents fought when; the Thespians and Arcadians are shown in the line only to illustrate the rotation [hdt].

phases.label: Lamp-lighting
phases.title: Ephialtes leads Hydarnes out
phases.text: Ephialtes, a Malian, tells Xerxes about the path over the mountain. 'About the time when the lamps are lit' Hydarnes leaves the camp with his men. The path begins at the Asopus, where it flows out of its gorge; it is called the Anopaea, like the mountain [hdt]. Herodotus says the Malians had once led the Thessalians against the Phocians by it [hdt]. Diodorus says 20,000 men went [diod].
tactic: Turning movement
A force marches round the enemy's flank by a route he thinks too hard or too little known, to arrive in his rear.
events: The Persians cross the Asopus; the Anopaea begins [hdt]

phases.label: Night march
phases.title: Through the oak woods in the dark
phases.text: The column climbs all night, with the Oetaean mountains on its right and the Trachinian on its left [hdt]. In the Greek camp the seer Megistias reads death at dawn in the sacrifices, and deserters come in before daylight with the news that the Persians are going round [hdt]. Diodorus names one, Tyrrhastiadas of Cyme [diod].
tactic: Turning movement
A night march over a mountain path is slow and blind; everything depends on the guide.
events: Megistias and deserters warn the Greeks [hdt]
phases.debate: Herodotus fixes only the ends: from the Asopus to Alpenos [hdt]. This route goes up past the Kalkomata spring and Paleo-Eleftherochori and along the upper Asopus meadows, where most modern topographers put it (Gordon's line on Kromayer's map; Wallace 1980; Pritchett) [kv] [standrews]. Kromayer's own route is shorter: Alt-Damasta, along the north side of Lithitza, to Alt-Drakospilia. Leake and Grundy go by the Panagia monastery [kv]. Pausanias says Hydarnes used the easier of two paths, 'through the territory of the Aenianians' [paus]. The route shown is about 18 km; a column could cover it at about 2 km/h in a summer night.

phases.label: Dawn on the summit
phases.title: The Phocians hear the leaves
phases.text: At dawn the Persians reach the top. The air is still and the ground deep in oak leaves, so the Phocians hear them coming and snatch up their arms. Hydarnes fears they are Spartans until Ephialtes tells him otherwise. Under a shower of arrows the Phocians fall back to the summit to make a stand, but the Persians ignore them and hurry down the mountain [hdt]. Day-watchers run down to the Greeks with the news [hdt].
tactic: Exposed outpost
A detachment guarding a remote approach is surprised and stands aside; once the outpost has failed, the main position is turned.
events: Phocians surprised on the Sastani saddle [hdt] [kv]
The Phocians make for the peak [hdt]
phases.debate: The Phocian post is placed on the Sastani saddle, following Kromayer, who sends every route but Munro's over it [kv]. Others put the encounter on the height north-east of the Nevropoli lake [standrews].

phases.label: Dismissal
phases.title: Leonidas sends the allies away
phases.text: A council divides the Greeks. Most march off to their cities; Herodotus thinks Leonidas sent them away himself to save them, keeping the Spartans, the Thespians (who refused to go) and the Thebans (held as hostages) [hdt]. Leonidas also tries to send away Megistias, who stays and sends his son instead [hdt]. Xerxes pours libations at sunrise and waits, as Ephialtes advises [hdt].
tactic: Rearguard
A force sacrifices itself to hold the enemy while the rest of the army gets away.
events: Council: the allies go, the Thespians and Thebans stay [hdt]
phases.debate: Diodorus has the council at midnight, keeps only the Lacedaemonians and Thespians (about 500), and sends them on a night attack on Xerxes' tent [diod]. That version is rejected here, as by most modern writers, in favour of Herodotus [stronk]. Which road the allies took is not recorded; the coast road east past Alpenoi, before the Immortals reached it, is assumed.

phases.label: The last sortie
phases.title: Into the broader part of the pass
phases.text: At 'the hour when the market fills' Xerxes advances. Knowing they are to die, the Greeks go out much further than before into the broader part of the pass. Many Persians, driven on by officers with whips, are pushed into the sea or trampled. With most of their spears broken, the Greeks fight with swords. Leonidas falls, and so do Abrocomes and Hyperanthes, brothers of Xerxes. The Greeks drive the enemy back four times and recover the king's body [hdt].
tactic: Frontal assault
A huge force pushed head-on into a narrow front pays heavily for every metre.
events: Leonidas falls; four rallies over his body [hdt]
phases.debate: Kromayer's map 7 and the Thermopylae museum both put this fight west of the narrows, near the old baths [kv] [museum]. Diodorus's night raid on the royal tent is a different, later tradition [diod] [stronk].

phases.label: The kolonos
phases.title: The last stand
phases.text: When word comes that Hydarnes is behind them, the survivors fall back past the wall to the hillock in the entrance to the pass, 'where the stone lion now stands for Leonidas'. The Thebans break away and surrender. On the hillock the rest fight with daggers, hands and teeth until they are buried under missiles; some Persians break down the wall in front while others close in from all sides [hdt]. Marinatos's 1939 excavation found masses of arrowheads on Kolonos [wp].
tactic: Last stand
Cut off front and rear, the remnant takes the strongest ground left and fights until overwhelmed.
phases.debate: The hillock is identified with Kolonos, where Marinatos found the arrowheads [wp]. Kromayer labels a hill farther east as the Leonidashügel but writes that the end came 'probably on hill 2', which matches Kolonos; Grundy says the 'second mound' [kv] [grundy]. Herodotus gives 20,000 Persian dead and 4,000 Greek bodies, including helots; most modern writers accept roughly 2,000 Greek dead [hdt] [wp].

units.name: Spartans (Leonidas)
units.note: The 300, chosen from men who had sons. They were outside the wall when Xerxes' scout rode up, used feigned flights against the Immortals, and died in the sortie and on the kolonos; only Aristodemos and Pantites, who were away, survived [hdt].

units.name: Helots and Lacedaemonian light troops
units.note: Herodotus mentions helots among the dead and a helot leading the blind Eurytos to the fight. The 900 (three per Spartan) is a modern inference, and so is their presence at the end [hdt] [wp].

units.name: Thespians (Demophilos)
units.note: The Thespians chose to stay with Leonidas on the last day and died with him; Dithyrambos was named the bravest of them [hdt].

units.name: Thebans (Leontiades)
units.note: Herodotus says Leonidas kept them as hostages; they fought for a while on day 3, then broke away while the others made for the hillock and surrendered. Some were killed as they came over; the rest were branded [hdt].

units.name: Tegeans
units.note: Arcadian contingent of 500 [hdt]. Which contingents stood in the line on day 1 is not recorded; this one is shown in support during the Immortals' attack. It was dismissed on day 3 [hdt].

units.name: Mantineans
units.note: Arcadian contingent of 500 [hdt]; dismissed on day 3 [hdt].

units.name: Orchomenians and other Arcadians
units.note: 120 from Orchomenos and 1,000 from the rest of Arcadia [hdt]. They are shown taking a turn in the line on day 2, when 'they fought successively each in turn' [hdt].

units.name: Corinthians, Phliasians and Mycenaeans
units.note: 400 Corinthians, 200 from Phlius and 80 from Mycenae [hdt]; dismissed on day 3 [hdt].

units.name: Opuntian Locrians
units.note: Herodotus says they came 'in full force' without a number; Diodorus gives 1,000 and Pausanias up to 6,000. The lowest figure is shown [hdt] [diod] [paus].

units.name: Phocians on the mountain
units.note: They volunteered to guard the Anopaea path. Surprised at dawn by the noise of the Persians in the oak leaves, and under arrows, they fell back to the peak expecting to be attacked; the Persians ignored them [hdt]. Their post on the Sastani saddle follows Kromayer [kv].

units.name: Medes
units.note: Sent first with the Cissians, with orders to take the Greeks alive; they lost heavily all day and came on again on day 2 [hdt]. Diodorus adds the kinsmen of the Marathon dead [diod]. Their strength is not recorded.

units.name: Cissians
units.note: Attacked alongside the Medes on day 1 [hdt]; Diodorus has them, with Sacae, relieving the Medes [diod]. Their strength is not recorded.

units.name: Immortals (Hydarnes), guided by Ephialtes
units.note: Persia's royal guard, 10,000 strong by Herodotus's count. They failed against the wall on day 1. At lamp-lighting on day 2 they left with Ephialtes over the Anopaea path, reached the summit at dawn, brushed the Phocians aside and came down behind the Greeks [hdt]. The route is a reconstruction [kv] [standrews].

units.name: Xerxes' assault columns (day 3)
units.note: Sent in at 'the hour when the market fills', driven forward with whips; many were pushed into the sea or trampled. Two of Xerxes' brothers, Abrocomes and Hyperanthes, fell [hdt]. The strength is illustrative.

units.name: Persian main army in camp
units.note: The rest of the army, including the cavalry, stayed on the Trachinian plain, where it could not be used in the pass [hdt] [kv]. Herodotus's millions are discarded; 120,000 in all is the low end of modern estimates [wp].

hq.name: Leonidas
hq.note: King of Sparta and commander of the whole force; he fell in the day-3 sortie, and the Spartans recovered his body after a struggle [hdt].

hq.name: Xerxes
hq.note: He watched from a seat and is said to have leapt up three times in fear for his army; on day 3 he poured libations at sunrise before the attack [hdt]. His viewpoint is not recorded and is placed illustratively.

hq.name: Hydarnes and Ephialtes
hq.note: Hydarnes commanded the Immortals; Ephialtes son of Eurydemos, a Malian, guided them [hdt].
